overview.summary: Court reporters create exact written records of what is said in court hearings, depositions and meetings, using specialist machines or recording and transcription methods. Methods differ by country.
overview.problems: They provide accurate official records that judges, lawyers and the public can rely on.
overview.worksWith: Judges, lawyers, witnesses, court staff and the people involved in cases.
overview.workplaces: Courtrooms, law offices and meeting rooms, plus remote or captioning work for broadcasts and events.

timeline.title: Preparation
timeline.description: The reporter reads case names, terms and speakers' names and tests equipment.

timeline.title: Recording every word
timeline.description: The reporter captures speech accurately and keeps up with fast speakers, using shorthand machines or approved methods.
timeline.why: The record may be used in appeals.

timeline.title: Asking for clarification
timeline.description: The reporter politely interrupts when something cannot be heard or understood.
timeline.why: An accurate record matters more than flow.

timeline.title: Editing the transcript
timeline.description: The reporter checks, corrects and formats the full record.

timeline.title: Delivering and certifying
timeline.description: The reporter provides the transcript and signs that it is accurate.
timeline.why: The certificate lets courts trust the record.

timeline.title: Captioning and other work
timeline.description: Some reporters caption live broadcasts or events.
timeline.why: Live captions make events accessible to more people.

responsibilities: Preparing names and terms in advance
challenges: Intense concentration is needed for long periods.
Reaching very high speed and accuracy takes years of training.
Digital recording and speech-to-text tools are changing the field.
Qualification and certification rules vary by country.
workEnvironment: Courtrooms and meeting rooms for live work, and offices or home for editing transcripts. Hours depend on hearings and deadlines. Some reporters work freelance or in captioning.
rewards: Playing a key role in justice
tradeoffs: Pay and demand that vary by country and setting

activity.title: Transcribe a short recording accurately
steps: Ask a friend or family member who agrees to read aloud a short passage they wrote for one minute, and record it with a phone.
Play it back and type exactly what is said, including pauses.
Check your transcript by listening again and fix mistakes.
Count the words and errors and work out your accuracy.
Note whether the concentration felt interesting.
activity.outcome: You practise careful listening, fast accurate typing and checking your work.
activity.safety: Record only people who agree, use their own text and not copyrighted material, and delete recordings when you finish if the speaker asks.

source: Written by Futurixia from general knowledge of how this profession works. It is illustrative and is not based on interviews or surveys.
